newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian prime minister sets June 2 election date.
newsitem.headline: Canadian prime minister sets June 2 election date.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien decided on Sunday to call a June 2 general election, 17 months before the required date, in order to cash in on a solid Liberal lead in the polls.

"I have just met with the Governor-General, who has issued a writ dissolving Parliament. A general election will be held on June 2," said a text of Chretien's remarks distributed ahead of a planned noon (1600 GMT) meeting with the governor-general.
"I will be asking Canadians to give the Liberal Party a new mandate to build on the record of the last four years," Chretien said in the prepared text.

In fact, he has only governed for 3-1/2 years, but has such a lead in the polls over a badly split opposition that another majority government would be assured if voting trends held until election day.
Chretien, 63, tried to show that relief was ahead after the tough deficit slashing his government had implemented. "Today we see that the light at the end of the tunnel is growing brighter," he said.

But he refused to yield to the calls for tax cuts being issued by the Conservative and Reform parties on his right, saying it would risk all the gains Canada had made "to introduce a tax cut before the country can afford one."
Under Canada's system, the prime minister must ask the governor-general to dissolve Parliament so elections can be called.

Chretien had been widely expected to issue the call on Sunday, the only question having built over the last couple of days being whether he might postpone it by a week or two because of major flooding in Manitoba in central Canada.

An Angus Reid poll published on Saturday gave the Liberals a 24-point lead amongst decided voters over their nearest rivals, the Conservatives, and a Gallup Canada poll on Friday put them 40 points ahead.
A right-wing split between the populist Reform Party and the then-ruling Conservatives in 1993 enabled the Liberals to sweep to a crushing majority of 177 out of 295 seats in the House of Commons.

The opposition is further split with the Bloc Quebecois pushing for the separatist vote in Quebec and the New Democractic Party (NDP) angling for the left with calls for more spending and None are registering more than 18 percent in the latest national polls, though in Quebec and the West respectively the Bloc and Reform have concentrated strength that makes it likely they will still win a substantial number of seats.
Some pollsters say the Bloc could again return as the official opposition despite its desire to take mainly francophone Quebec out of Canada.
But about one-third of those polled are undecided, and Canadian voters have showed tremendous volatility in recent years, giving Chretien's rivals a glimmer of hope.

All sides have criticised Chretien's cuts to Canada's cherished health care, prompting him to declare in his remarks that he needed a mandate to "see the job through ... to make important investments in our health care system."

On the right, besides tax cuts, he is also vulnerable on law and order, gun control and family values, and on the left on topics like day care and a large range of government programmes like the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation.
Conservative leader Jean Charest kicked off his campaign in Ottawa on Sunday morning with a jab at Chretien for talking about possibly raising spending once the deficit is licked.
"The great rule of Jean Chretien -- it's written on his door: 'If you send it, we'll spend it,'" Charest thundered.

Reform held a campaign convention in Toronto all weekend, and its leader Preston Manning charged on Saturday that the Liberals in Parliament had tried to stick false labels on any who disagreed with them.

"Anyone who attempts to defend the traditional family is homophobic. Anyone who demands law and order is extremist. Anyone who questions the wisdom of their national unity is a traitor to Canada," Manning said.
Chretien scheduled a rally in his Quebec hometown of Shawinigan for Sunday evening and a gruelling schedule from coast to coast for the week ahead.
